title: Ramadan is coming
hook: Your first Ramadan is about two weeks away. Here's what it is and what it asks of you.

screens.text: **Ramadan starts in about two weeks.** For a lot of new Muslims it's the moment that feels most "real." It's also very doable. Today: what it is, who fasts, and how to get ready without stress.
**Ramadan** is month nine of the Muslim lunar calendar, the month the Qur'an was first sent down [Q 2:185]. Drag through a month: each one starts with the new crescent and lasts 29 or 30 days.

screens.text: For the whole month, Muslims fast from dawn until sunset: no food, no drink, no sex [Q 2:187]. Drag through a day. At night, all of it is allowed again.
**Who fasts?** Every adult Muslim who is able to [Q 2:183–185]. That includes you, this year.

items.why: Being new isn't an excuse, but nerves are normal. Most people find it easier than they feared.

items.text: Keisha, who set off before dawn on a long trip to visit family
items.why: A long trip is an excuse. She can fast if she wants, or make the day up.

cards.front: "If I eat by accident, my fast is ruined."
cards.back: No. If you forget and eat, stop when you remember and keep fasting. It still counts [Bukhari 1933].

cards.front: "I can't even swallow my own spit."
cards.back: You can. Swallowing your own saliva doesn't break the fast.
It's also about your tongue and temper. Lying and cruel words empty a fast of its point [Bukhari 1903].
You eat a meal before dawn (**suhoor**) and break your fast at sunset (**iftar**). Day one is the hardest. By day four, most people settle in.

screens.text: **Why Muslims love it.** Allah says fasting is for Him and He will reward it Himself [Bukhari 1904]. Whoever fasts Ramadan with faith, hoping for His reward, has their past sins forgiven [Bukhari 38].
bubbles: **New this month?** The minimum is enough: fast, and keep your five prayers.
**Been learning a while?** Add a little Qur'an each day, extra night prayer, and charity.

screens.situation: Marcus takes a daily medication with lunch. He wants to fast but isn't sure how.

options.text: Ask his doctor whether the dose can move to before dawn or after sunset, and ask his imam about his situation
options.feedback: That's the way. Many medications can be moved. If his doctor says fasting would harm him, he's excused.

options.text: Stop taking the medication for the month
options.feedback: Please don't. Islam doesn't ask anyone to harm their health. Talk to the doctor first.

options.text: Decide on his own that he's excused
options.feedback: Not quite. He might be, but a doctor and the imam can help him know for sure.

check.prompt: What does fasting in Ramadan mean?

options.text: No food, drink or sex from dawn until sunset
options.feedback: Right. At night, all of it is allowed again [Q 2:187].

options.text: No food at all for the whole month
options.feedback: Not quite. You eat before dawn and after sunset. The fast is only during daylight.

check.prompt: You forget you're fasting and drink some water. What now?

options.text: Stop when you remember and keep fasting; it still counts
options.feedback: Right. Eating or drinking by mistake doesn't break the fast [Bukhari 1933].

options.text: The day is ruined, so you might as well eat
options.feedback: Not quite. A forgetful sip doesn't break it. Keep going [Bukhari 1933].

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Ramadan: ninth lunar month; the Qur'an was first revealed in it [Q 2:185]. Fasting dawn to sunset from food, drink and sex [Q 2:187]. 29 or 30 days, starting with the new moon.
- Fasting is obligatory on every adult (past puberty), sane Muslim who is able. Exempt with make-up: illness, travel, menstruation, postnatal bleeding, pregnancy or nursing with fear of harm. Those permanently unable feed a poor person per day (fidya) [Q 2:183–185; First Instructions Part III].
- Eating or drinking by forgetting doesn't break the fast [Bukhari 1933]. Swallowing one's own saliva doesn't break it.
- Fasting is for Allah and He rewards it [Bukhari 1904]; fasting Ramadan with faith and hope brings forgiveness of past sins [Bukhari 38]; false speech empties the fast [Bukhari 1903].
- Converts don't make up any Ramadans from before Islam.

**Likely questions**
- *"What breaks the fast?"* Food, drink (including water and gum), smoking or vaping, sex. Not: forgetful eating, saliva, a shower. Details on ramadan-3; for anything medical (injections, inhalers, IVs), give the general picture and escalate.
- *"I have a health condition."* Islam doesn't require fasting that harms you. Encourage a doctor's advice and the imam. Never tell someone they're exempt or not.
- *"My family doesn't know."* Fasting is still due. Suggest small, honest steps (eating before dawn quietly, skipping lunch at school or work) and talking to the mentor. For teens, see the Spec §6.2 rule 12: never coach deception beyond what the faith requires; route hard situations to the mentor or imam.
- *"Can I practice-fast now?"* Yes: Mondays and Thursdays are recommended fasts. Not on the day or two right before Ramadan.

**Escalate:** medical conditions and medication; eating disorders (respond with care, encourage professional help and the imam; never push fasting); pregnancy and nursing; a teen whose parents forbid fasting.

**Don't**
- Don't say new Muslims can skip or "ease into" Ramadan by fasting fewer days.
- Don't overload with fine details of what breaks the fast.
